corrections.issue: Speaker is the listener Paul, whose written question Niels reads out, not Niels; the Moskowitz et al. (2012) reading is the listener's.
corrections.fix: Listener Paul (read by Niels): Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012) find returns in years 2 to 5 are negatively related to subsequent returns, so an absolute long-term mean reversion signal might raise standalone Sharpe.

corrections.issue: Speaker is the listener Paul (question read by Niels), describing Rob's strategy in his book; not Niels's own view.
corrections.fix: Listener Paul (read by Niels): Rob's relative five-year mean reversion strategy in Advanced Futures Trading Strategies has a negative standalone Sharpe but improves a baseline trend-plus-carry portfolio.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker. Rob Carver is speaking here, continuing his explanation of the Sharpe versus skew trade-off (the sentence runs across the C16/C17 boundary); Niels does not speak until later in C17.
corrections.fix: Rob Carver: option selling (extreme) and equity market neutral (less extreme) strategies have good Sharpe ratios but negative skew, unlike trend following which has positive skew.

corrections.issue: Probable wrong speaker. 'I do agree with you that actually a price-based strategy that doesn't care about is it the right value or not' answers Niels's point about trust erosion and the value-price disconnect, so it reads as Rob agreeing with Niels.
corrections.fix: Rob Carver (probable): in a world where price and value are disconnected, a price-following strategy such as trend following is a good thing to hold in a portfolio.
